candidate.description: An owning runtime (for example an AGS supervisor) spawns `codex app-server` itself and keeps the child process handle. It sends JSON-RPC on the child's stdin, starts turns with turn/start, and reads the TurnStartResponse and turn/started notifications (thread_id, turn.id) from the child's stdout pipe.

claimedOwnership.process: The supervisor holds the process handle returned by its own spawn call.
claimedOwnership.instance: The single stdio connection (ConnectionOrigin::Stdio) exists only for the supervisor's pipes.
claimedOwnership.turn: The supervisor originates turn/start and receives the turn object on the same pipe.

candidate.requiredForAuthority: The supervisor's stdout-pipe read side must accept bytes only from the app-server process itself. Any principal able to write JSON-RPC lines into that pipe could forge turn/started notifications or responses.

trace.finding: The app-server default transport is stdio://. The stdio connection opens with origin Stdio and auth None, reads JSON-RPC lines from the process's own stdin, and writes to the process's own stdout. TurnStartResponse carries `turn` and TurnStartedNotification carries `thread_id` and `turn`. The candidate therefore delivers process, instance, and turn facts to the supervisor over the supervisor's pipes.
trace.source: transport/mod.rs:123; cli/src/main.rs:568 (app-server --listen default_value); stdio.rs:56-59,73,87; turn.rs:268-270,492-495; installed `codex app-server --help`

trace.finding: On Windows, command hooks are spawned by run_command through tokio::process::Command with piped stdio. When a JobObject exists, JobObject::spawn_contained is used, which still calls command.spawn(). The pipe-based tool spawn paths (core spawn_child_async and utils/pty pipe spawn) also use Command::spawn.

Rust std 1.95.0 on Windows defaults `inherit_handles: true` and passes it as bInheritHandles to CreateProcessW. It attaches a PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE list only when the caller supplies one. The Command paths in step 2 supply none, so every inheritable handle in the app-server process is inherited by those children, not just their own piped stdio.

Across all non-test codex-rs/*.rs files at the pinned commit, no code clears HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT, calls SetStdHandle, or calls Command inherit_handles(false). Every SetHandleInformation call sets HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT on. PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST is used only by windows-sandbox-rs for sandboxed launches. ConPTY launches pass bInheritHandles=0. pre_main_hardening_windows is an unimplemented TODO.
trace.source: grep over the pinned archive (SetHandleInformation|HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT|inherit_handles\(|SetStdHandle|PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST); DuplicateHandle uses were also checked (exec-server sandboxed_file_open.rs, windows-sandbox-rs elevated/runner_client.rs and setup_launch.rs) and are unrelated to app-server stdio;windows-sandbox-rs/process.rs:76,131-143; proc_thread_attr.rs:61-67; psuedocon.rs:189-200 (bInheritHandles argument 0); process-hardening/lib.rs:120-121

forgeryRefutation.forgerClass: Command-hook child processes and non-sandboxed, pipe-spawned tool processes launched by the same app-server. These are the same principal class whose origin claims W06-a-codex must not trust.
forgeryRefutation.path: The app-server's stdout write handle is the supervisor-created pipe end. Nothing in the pinned source removes it from inheritance, and the hook spawn path creates children with bInheritHandles=TRUE and no handle list. Conditional on the osPremises below, a hook child obtains a handle to the supervisor's read pipe: through inheritance, where it must still find the handle value, for example by enumerating small handle values; or through PROCESS_DUP_HANDLE duplication. It can then write a well-formed JSON-RPC line such as a forged turn/started notification. The supervisor cannot tell those bytes from app-server output because the stdio connection has no per-message authentication (auth None). The unconditional finding is narrower: the pinned source contains no forgery-resistant boundary for this channel.

osPremises.premise: An inherited handle refers to the same object and has the same value and access privileges. Inheritability is controlled per handle (SetHandleInformation), and CreateProcess with bInheritHandles=TRUE passes all inheritable handles unless PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST restricts them.
A handle that app-server received by inheritance keeps its inheritable flag unless app-server clears it, so app-server's own bInheritHandles=TRUE spawns pass it on.
osPremises.source: Not stated verbatim on the Microsoft page above. Recorded as an unobserved OS premise.

osPremises.premise: Independent of inheritance, a same-user, same-integrity process such as an unsandboxed hook child can normally open the app-server process with PROCESS_DUP_HANDLE and duplicate its stdout handle, because the pinned Windows process hardening is an unimplemented TODO.
osPremises.source: process-hardening/lib.rs:120-121 plus Windows default process security model

forgeryRefutation.why_not_dependent_on_forbidden_execution: The determination does not need a live forgery. An authority channel requires a boundary that excludes the forger class. The pinned source contains no such boundary on Windows: no inheritance clearing, no handle list for hook spawns, no process hardening, and no message authentication on stdio. A live app-server or hook run could only confirm an exploit and could not create the missing boundary. On the stdio transport the supervisor cannot supply that boundary alone: handles passed through STARTUPINFO must be inheritable, and changing the child's own std handles would require code inside the child. The OS premises are recorded separately and not claimed as observed.

determination.scope: Candidate SUPERVISOR_OWNED_APP_SERVER_STDIO; Windows; installed codex-cli 0.155.1 (SHA-256 eba0f32c…6316) pinned to be2951ea
determination.reason: The supervisor does own the process, the stdio connection, and the turn requests. However, the pinned Windows source provides no boundary that keeps same-app-server hook or tool descendants out of that stdio channel, and it has no per-message authentication. The pinned source therefore has no forgery-resistant boundary. The concrete exploit path is conditional on the recorded OS premises. No verifiable host-origin authority channel exists for this candidate.
determination.priorityApplied: Rule (1) BLOCKED_EVIDENCE does not apply because the determination does not depend on a forbidden execution. Rule (2) VERIFIED_AUTHORITY_CHANNEL does not apply because the forgery refutation fails. Rule (3) AUTHORITY_CHANNEL_ABSENT applies because absence of the required boundary is shown from the pinned source.
determination.progressMapping: May request investigation Progress COMPLETED. The W06-a-codex product gate accepts only VERIFIED_AUTHORITY_CHANNEL, so W06-a-codex stays BLOCKED and no product gate opens.
determination.productDisposition: No product hook, configuration, or code change. Do not promote existing candidates.
determination.falsifier: This conclusion would be overturned by a pinned v0.155.1 source location, or an allowed static check of the installed release, showing either of the following: app-server clears inheritance on, or otherwise isolates, its stdio handles before spawning hook or tool children; or the stdio connection carries per-message authentication that a descendant cannot produce. A turn id field, a matching PID, or the codex executable name alone would not overturn it.

proposedSeparateContract.summary: If AGS needs owning-runtime authority for Codex, open a separate implementation contract. It would evaluate a supervisor-created channel that descendants cannot reach, for example a supervisor-listened ws:// or unix:// endpoint with a per-launch secret, or a named pipe with a restrictive DACL. It would also need forged-line and duplicate-handle falsification tests and an explicit decision on how that authority reaches AGS hook enforcement.
